description: UVM Students Offer Real-World Climate Recommendations to Vermont Town is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Vermont Agency or Natural Resources Department of Fish and Wildlife; Vermont Climate Action Office; Vermont Agency of Transportation. The town of Underhill, Vermont, is considering climate-change recommendations developed and presented by some intrepid University of Vermont (UVM) students. These students worked in collaboration with town, state, and federal agencies this past fall to come up with a plan to aid their town in natural-hazard mitigation in the face of our changing climate. Coverage: Vermont (2023). The toolkit gives Vermont as the location, 2023 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
